events.title: Iran War Escalation
events.summary: The Iran war has revealed the limits of US power and the waning geopolitical influence. The conflict has also shown the military strength of the US, but its inability to achieve a decisive victory. The war has significant implications for the global economy and trade.
events.reasoning: The Iran war has disrupted global oil supplies, leading to higher prices. The conflict has also weakened the US dollar, making emerging markets more vulnerable to economic shocks. As a result, investors should short emerging markets and buy oil-related assets.

timeFrame.note: Monitor oil prices and US dollar movements

events.exitStrategy: Exit when oil prices stabilize or the US dollar strengthens

events.title: US Inflation Rate
events.summary: The US inflation rate has been rising, driven by higher oil prices and a strong labor market. The Federal Reserve has indicated that it may raise interest rates to combat inflation.
events.reasoning: The rising inflation rate makes Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) more attractive, while long-term Treasury bonds become less appealing. Investors should buy TIPS and short long-term Treasury bonds.

timeFrame.note: Monitor inflation data and Fed statements

events.exitStrategy: Exit when inflation data shows signs of slowing down
